thread:
Maya L.: quick update — ran a batch of occupancy / shared-mem experiments on A100-80GB. saw a perf valley at seq_len ~384 that doesn't line up with naive occupancy calc.
Andre P.: interesting. valley meaning tokens/s drops relative to 256 and 512?
Maya L.: yes, 256 -> 384 drops ~18% throughput, then recovers at 512. weird. numbers below from benchbot.
BenchBot: perf summary (avg over 30 runs):
```
seq_len  tokens/s  latency_ms  occupancy  smem_per_block  regs_per_thread
256      540k      12.3        0.78       48KB            64
384      440k      15.0        0.74       60KB            78
512      560k      11.8        0.76       64KB            80
```
Maya L.: note smem_per_block jumps around 60KB at 384 due to extra staging buffer in tile loop (we added a small transpose path).
Samir: that reg increase to 78 is suspicious — could be spilling/stack usage? did nvprof show spill/stores?
BenchBot: nvprof sample (kernel=attn_tiled): spill stores = 0.9% at 256, 4.7% at 384, 1.1% at 512.
Kai T.: that aligns with register pressure causing the compiler to allocate extra shared mem/temp storage maybe. Also warp occupancy drops when regs/thread crosses threshold. If we tune tile Y to reduce reg usage at 384 maybe it helps.
Andre P.: what's tile config used for the run?
Maya L.: current config: tile_m=64, tile_n=64, warp_splits=1, stage_buffers=2. launch params: 8 warps/block (i.e., 256 threads).
Samir: try lowering tile_m to 32 (fewer accumulators => fewer regs), or increase warps/block to 12 to spread reg pressure (if smem allows).
Maya L.: ok pushed a quick build with tile_m=32, warps/block=12. new numbers:
BenchBot: run results:
```
seq_len  tokens/s  latency_ms  occupancy  smem_per_block  regs_per_thread  spill%
384      510k      12.6        0.86       44KB            56               0.8%
```
Maya L.: big win. occupancy up, spill down, throughput almost back to 256 baseline.
Kai T.: so root cause looked like tile config oscillating register usage around compiler threshold for spill; sequence length changed staging behaviour which pushed patterns over that cliff. Good catch.
Andre P.: for autotuner, we should include seq_len as a dimension or at least a bucket. pick kernel variant based on seq_len range [<=256, 257-416, >416]. 384 sits in mid bucket where different tile shapes win.
Samir: agree. Also track regs/thread and smem_per_block during profiling; autotuner objective should prefer configs that minimize spill% first, then tokens/s. Spills introduce nondeterministic latency jumps.
Maya L.: maybe add a cheap static heuristic in kernel selection: if compiled_regs_per_thread > 72 && seq_len in [300,420] prefer tile_m=32 variant. That avoids running autotune in hot path.
Andre P.: can we get compilation-time estimates? rocm/cuda have PTX reg count output. benchtool can parse PTX/SASS to extract "used registers" and smem. do that in model onboarding.
ci-bot: triggered autotune job #4512 for model=gpt-small on a100-80gb (seq_buckets=[128,256,384,512]) — results will post in thread.
BenchBot: autotune #4512 top candidates: variant-A(tile64,warp1) for <=256, variant-B(tile32,warp2) for 257-416, variant-C(tile64,q2) for >416.
Kai T.: one more note — watch shared-memory bank conflicts on tile_m=32 path. microbench shows +6% cycles lost to bank conflict when we align stride poorly. use padding or warp-specialized loads.
Maya L.: added 8-byte padding to per-warp buffers; re-run shows conflict drop and tokens/s stable.
Samir: small action items: (1) add seq_len bucket to kernel selector, (2) emit reg/smem/spill metrics from benchtool, (3) autotuner objective: minimize spill% then latency, (4) add unit test simulating seq=384 to avoid regressions.
Maya L.: i'll open a PR with heuristics + bench outputs. dropping p99 traces too to show variability.
Andre P.: thanks — can we also add a note in runtime docs about "compiler cliff" and why tile shapes affect register pressure? quick paragraph should save future confusion.
Maya L.: yep. will add docs and mark with examples.
Kai T.: awesome. :thumbsup:
